t_957ca870.title: FORK FEATURE: deliberate single-sub worker pin (--pin-sub <reason>) — restore the pin-a-worker-to-claude-bpx-N capability that hermes-agent#1116 removed with a blanket refusal; keep sub 0 + pre-rename aliases + unadmitted subs refused; document everywhere (Ace 09-27 08:31)
t_957ca870.body:
origin: discord Daemonarchy / #ci-overflow-merge-attribution (1551233545887031418) · session 20260923_104227_84053430 · 2026-09-27

Ace 2026-09-27 08:31 PT: "I thought we built the fork feature for that... If we've never done that, spec it out and do it as a fork feature and document it everywhere. It's a really desired feature."

HISTORY (Apollo 08:3x): pinning a worker card to one sub DID work until yesterday. `kanban set-model <card> --provider claude-bpx-N` routed the worker to that sub (t_246ce7d6 "direct-pin rider shows hop on sub N", t_89805da4 "Fable on claude-bpx-25"). Fork PR ANG-Ventures/hermes-agent#1116 (merged 2026-09-26 15:42Z, card t_141135aa, Ace 09-25) removed it with a BLANKET refusal: hermes_cli/model_policy.py SINGLE_SUB_PIN_RE / pinned_sub_provider_error refuses every claude-(apx|bpx)-N and every pre-rename alias, in every route writer (create_task, set_model_override + batch, set_task_model, set_lane_model_override, lane-model CLI), with NO override flag. The incident it fixed was real but narrower: cards/lanes pinned to claude-apx-0 (= Ace's PERSONAL Mac sub, also reachable via the alias claude-api-proxy) put workers on his personal sub: 95x 429 + 46x 401 in one day. #1116 fixed the alias/personal-sub hole by banning all pins.

Today it bit: Ace asked for Fable on claude-bpx-24 (idle, full bars) for t_887f9584; set-model refused, Apollo had to run it as a cron/subagent outside kanban.

SPEC (write it with ang-spec first, then implement; one PR on the fork, branch from fork/main):
1. Explicit opt-in pin: `kanban set-model <card> --provider claude-bpx-N --model <m> --pin-sub "<reason>"` (also create-task and lane-model). Without --pin-sub the #1116 refusal text stays exactly as is.
2. Always refused, even with --pin-sub: claude-apx-0 / claude-bpx-0 (Ace's personal Mac sub) and every pre-rename alias (claude-api-proxy, claude-bridge, -fN...). Refuse a sub that is not admitted for worker traffic (burn-in / not in the pool registry, per fleet-model-governance + claude-pool-seat-admission-policy); read the same registry the pool uses, do not hand-list subs.
3. A pinned card bypasses the pool but not the governors: dispatch_load_gate, provider cooldown for THAT sub (429/usage cap => card waits or falls back to claude-bpr only if --pin-sub-fallback was given; default = wait), and the flagship gate (--allow-flagship still required for Fable).
4. Visibility: `kanban show/list` print `[PIN claude-bpx-N: <reason>]`; the dispatcher log line shows `source=pin`; a daily lint lists live pins (so a forgotten pin cannot silently hog a sub, the #1116 failure mode).
5. Tests: refusal-without-flag unchanged (#1116 suite stays green); pin honored end to end (route == pinned provider); apx-0/alias refused WITH the flag; non-admitted sub refused; cooldown wait path. Mutation-proven.
6. DOCS, all in the same PR/wave: skills model-routing, kanban-swarm-operations, fleet-model-governance, claude-pool-seat-admission-policy; Obsidian `Claude Relay — System Overview` (worker pinning section) and `Kanban` docs; mem0 fact; `hermes kanban set-model --help`. Every place that today says "workers never pin a sub" must say "workers ride the pool by default; a pin needs --pin-sub <reason>, never sub 0, never an unadmitted sub".
Acceptance: `kanban set-model <scratch card> --provider claude-bpx-24 --model claude-fable-5-1 --allow-flagship x --pin-sub "test"` dispatches on claude-bpx-24 (aegis gateway.log route=claude-bpx-24 source=pin) and the same command without --pin-sub is refused with the #1116 text.

t_bbe0023c.title: claude-pool warm eligibility: skip seats with an active/recent model-scope cap for the request's model
t_bbe0023c.body:
Origin: t_3d5af176 (warm-seat P2 enforce readout). Filed per Apollo ruling 2026-09-27 08:3x PT. Repo: claude-pool. Apollo named ANG-Ventures/claude-pool; the P1 PRs landed as Kyzcreig/claude-pool#85, so confirm the canonical remote before opening the PR.

Problem: with warm_rank=enforce, the warm stage selects a session's warm seat even when that seat is currently model-capped for the request's model (fable). The call then eats a 429, and the retry lands cold.

Evidence (bpr, post-flip 2026-09-26 23:28:43 PT; source: ~/.hermes/scripts/warm-enforce-readout.py; full table in t_3d5af176 comment 13058, follow-up 13112):
- 7 of 47 changed picks returned `route 429`: 6 of 11 on bpr and 1 of 36 on apr. All 6 bpr failures were fable.
- Each failed bpr pick went to a seat that had a model-scope fable `capped` 429 within the preceding 2–17 minutes:
  - vps-18: cap 23:38:56, pick 23:56:07
  - vps-2: cap 00:37:58, pick 00:40:15
  - vps-21: cap 01:18:58, pick 01:21:58
  - vps-1: cap 04:57:16, then 05:00:31; picks 05:00:29, 05:02:32, 05:32:22
- The next call after each failure read cold: 0.0–0.33, against 0.98+ for served warm picks.

Fix: warm eligibility (the WarmMap / warm_rank stage) must exclude a seat that has an active model-scope cap for the request's model, or a cap more recent than the pool's cap cooldown. The seat then falls through to stage1, as it does today when no warm seat exists. The exclusion must be model-scoped: a fable cap must not exclude the seat for opus.

Acceptance:
1. Regression test replaying the vps-1 sequence (model-scope fable capped, then a warm pick for the same fable session). It must be RED on pre-fix HEAD and GREEN after. Paste both runs.
2. Test that a cap on another model does not exclude the seat.
3. Emit a warm_* log field or reason (e.g. `warm_skip: model_capped`) so the readout can count skips.
4. CI green. Deploy is Apollo's job; do not kickstart relays.
